closed_findings.disposition: Base and each custom scene definition retain object facts captured at that read. Core announces its actual unsorted custom-file walk, verifies each opened scene/directory at its announced position, and queries that definition. Host inventory/base answers do not require any alternative sorted custom history; final store replays the announced order with original per-directory name-history resets.

Host replace_object and Core reset retain culling_normals_offset, the field original read_object never assigns; typed carry checks reject disagreement. The distinguishing parser fixture uses nonzero previous values for a common row, a hex override and the first custom replacement, and distinguishes a fresh second row.

One provider announcement is sequential, unique and bounded at 4096 entries before mutation. Its closed state is final; late, repeated-end, duplicate, out-of-sequence and domain errors are refused. Versioned wrappers and the C/Rust/Lua transport forward definition and directory fields.

After the unchanged actual custom traversal, Core requires every announced position consumed and no outstanding read. Unsupported-version files consume explicit skip positions and claim no object read; the original version -1 through -3 conditional and skip body remain. The final test anchors the actual function definition, not its forward declaration, preserving the branch assertions.

Inventory-first bootstrap reads no custom scene payload. A real-parser fixture distinguishes sorted-history room exhaustion from a fitting announced history. The provider pins its installation as an absolute path when selected and uses that path for replay, rather than re-reading mutable root text after native chdir. Final answers cannot fall back to a different order after failed replay.

Public animation answers carry truthful logical names, never file animation indices. The original Core add_new_animation/T2 policy resolves valid unknown names as before. Malformed text remains a refusal. Both corrected default retail list captures now literally match the retained originals.

Feature-only hooks record successful file reads, actual allocation/append/final pointer/count provenance before list entries are read or hashed. The strict four-row horizon grammar accounts for the ninth rows_replaced counter and current described rows as filled minus replaced. Unsupported backing is not labelled filled success.

FFI test initializers carry role, definition and bounded key fields; lint complexity uses aliases without suppression. Changed-animation controls require a reached change, final definition and observed final Core list, and fail when unreached/unavailable/ignored.
